findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:662-670: the non-PLAN branch of the title/context-freeze refusal message ("first roll back to PLAN, then run lattice story_advance ... phase INIT") is inaccurate/impossible for the phases where it actually fires. titleContextProtectedPhases (line 651) includes INIT_CHECK, DEV, REVIEW, TEST, DONE. From REVIEW or TEST the machine only allows a rollback to DEV (machine.ts REVIEW/TEST states: START->DEV via canReenterDev), not directly to PLAN -- reaching PLAN needs a second hop (DEV->PLAN via REPLAN) that the message never mentions. From DONE there is NO rollback edge at all (machine.ts: DONE:{type:"final"}), so a title-edit attempt on a DONE story is told to do something structurally impossible. Only the DEV case (single REPLAN hop) matches the literal instruction. Severity medium because the refusal itself still correctly blocks the edit (no invariant break), but the recovery guidance it prints is factually wrong/misleading for REVIEW, TEST and DONE.

packages/main/src/tasks/plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts (whole file) + core/machine.ts canReopenToInitGuard/PLAN.on.REOPEN: checklist CHK-001 declares a must-priority adversarial verification intent (id CHK-001:adversarial:0) that reopen is "refused ... from any non-PLAN phase such as DEV or REVIEW", but no test in the diff (the new smoke only exercises reopen-refused-without-reason from PLAN and reopen-succeeds-from-PLAN) or elsewhere in packages/main/src/tasks exercises story_advance phase=INIT from DEV/REVIEW/TEST. Manual probing (story_advance phase=INIT from an INIT-phase story) only exercises the pre-existing generic self-transition guard, not the REOPEN remap path in transition-orchestrator.ts (which requires story.phase===PLAN to even engage). The guard is structurally correct on inspection (REOPEN is absent from the DEV/REVIEW/TEST xstate on-blocks and from the non-PLAN cases of canSendStoryEventWithoutSnapshotCan), so this is a coverage gap rather than a known defect -- but a declared must-priority adversarial item should have a concrete automated assertion rather than relying on code inspection alone.

CHK-001:adversarial:0 (must) is a compound claim: reopen refused when reason is missing AND refused from any non-PLAN phase such as DEV or REVIEW. plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts lines 162-166 (and its recorded verificationEvidence note) only exercise the missing-reason clause; the story never advances to DEV/REVIEW and attempts a reopen from there, and grep of packages/main/src for REOPEN/canReopenToInit turns up no other test covering the non-PLAN-phase refusal. The switch-case in machine.ts canSendStoryEventWithoutSnapshotCan (case PLAN: only place REOPEN is wired) makes it structurally likely to be correct, but this half of the must-priority intent has zero test evidence and a future refactor of that switch could silently break it with nothing to catch it.

CHK-002:edge:0 and CHK-002:adversarial:0 (both should-priority) have zero verificationEvidence and are not exercised anywhere in plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts: the smoke only bootstraps the worktree once from root (a fresh create, not a reuse) and then always calls story_advance from inside wt, so neither dev_start-invoked-from-main-repo-root-after-the-worktree-already-exists nor dev_start-after-the-worktree-directory-was-deleted is ever driven. Advisory per review rules (should, not must), but worth recording since these are the two edge/adversarial branches of the CHK-002 dev_start path fix and currently rely entirely on code-reading confidence, not test evidence.

doc-promise-undelivered: decision.json states the chosen design 'Preserves the INIT_CHECK scope-freeze invariant untouched' and preMortem #3 ('PLAN->INIT reopen is abused to escape a legitimately failing PLAN->DEV gate') concludes 'nothing downstream is bypassed' because 'the return trip re-enters the full INIT->INIT_CHECK gate (scope-freeze + INIT review)'. This promise is not delivered for a story that has already been through DEV: canReopenToInitGuard (packages/main/src/core/machine.ts:603-609) only checks story.phase==='PLAN' -- it never checks whether any checklist item.status is already 'done'. DEV->PLAN (REPLAN, lifecycle-registry.ts DEV->PLAN edge, effects:[]) is an existing, unguarded edge that does not reset checklist status. Chaining the pre-existing REPLAN with the new REOPEN therefore lets a maintainer land back at INIT -- the only phase where checklist_update permits title/context edits -- on a story whose checklist items are already 'done' (i.e. already implemented and, per checklist.ts's own comment, protected 'so the executor must not tamper with requirement definition during execution'). Verified live against the built CLI (packages/main/dist/cli.js): created a story, advanced to PLAN, force-set CHK-001.status='done' (simulating completed DEV work), ran story_advance phase=INIT with a valid reason (succeeded, no complaint about the done item), then checklist_update the title to an unrelated string (succeeded). Final state: CHK-001 status stayed 'done' while its title became completely disconnected from what was actually implemented/verified, with zero warning, no status reset, and no forced re-verification. None of the story's 3 documented preMortem scenarios, nor the new plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts, exercise a story with any 'done' checklist item, so this gap is untested and undocumented as an accepted risk. Suggested fix: canReopenToInitGuard (or the transition-orchestrator reopen branch) should refuse -- or require an explicit extra confirmation for -- a reopen when any checklist item.status is 'done', or checklist_update should reset a done item's status/verificationEvidence when its title/context changes at INIT.
findings.resolvedReason: transition-orchestrator.ts now resets any done/in_progress checklist item to pending as an effect of the REOPEN transition, so a reopened story cannot keep a done status while its requirement/title changes; the changed requirement must re-pass DEV/REVIEW. The round-trip smoke seeds a done CHK-001 and asserts it becomes pending after reopen. This makes the decision.json promise (preserves the INIT_CHECK scope-freeze invariant) actually delivered. commit 7dee7d7f89.
